articles.title: Hohe Millioneninvestition: Bundesregierung erwägt KI-Partnerschaft mit Nvidia
articles.preview: Die Bundesregierung plant eine strategische Partnerschaft mit dem US-Chiphersteller Nvidia. Ein dreistelliger Millionenbetrag soll in die Entwicklung von KI-gestützten Anwendungen fließen.

summary.t: Die Bundesregierung beabsichtigt, einen Investitionsbetrag im dreistelligen Millionenbereich zu tätigen. Diese Finanzierung soll primär der Förderung von Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) in Deutschland dienen.
Der Bund plant eine enge Zusammenarbeit mit dem US-Chiphersteller Nvidia.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Anthropic droht geringere Bewertung
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang urges U.S.-China dialogue on 'potentially dangerous' AI
articles.preview: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang believes open communication is crucial for navigating the risks of rapidly developing artificial intelligence. He is advocating for a U.S.-China dialogue to ensure AI’s safe advancement.

summary.t: Jensen Huang emphasized the necessity of Nvidia working with Chinese AI companies to monitor potential dangers associated with the technology. He stated that “dialogue” is the only viable approach, highlighting existing conversations with researchers in China. This stance directly contrasts with calls for increased regulation from organizations like OpenAI and Anthropic.

articles.title: Mehrere US-Bundesstaaten verklagen KI-Firma OpenAI
articles.preview: Acht US-Bundesstaaten haben OpenAI, den Entwickler von ChatGPT, wegen potenzieller Risiken verklagt. Die Klagen konzentrieren sich auf den Schutz der Nutzer und die Sicherheit der KI-Modelle.

summary.t: Acht US-Bundesstaaten haben gemeinsam Klagen gegen OpenAI eingereicht. Die Generalstaatsanwälte von Arizona, Arkansas, Iowa, Nebraska, Kansas, West Virginia, Idaho und Montana haben die Klagen in ihren jeweiligen Gerichten gestellt.
Die Bundesstaaten werfen OpenAI vor, nicht ausreichend für den Schutz der Nutzer zu sorgen. Sie argumentieren, ChatGPT könne Wahnvorstellungen verstärken und gefährliches Verhalten fördern.

articles.title: Anthropic taps nonprofits METR and SecureBio to help assess risks and safety practices
articles.preview: Anthropic is partnering with independent evaluators to assess its AI safety practices. This initiative follows a proposal to slow down model development and includes collaborations with organizations like METR and SecureBio.

summary.t: Anthropic has begun working with the nonprofit Model Evaluation and Threat Research (METR) and SecureBio. METR is considered a third-tier evaluator, granting its six employees access to Anthropic’s hardware, office spaces, and tools. These employees will analyze Anthropic’s risk levels and practices.

Anthropic is establishing a tiered system for evaluators. The first tier conducts narrowly scoped risk investigations, the second tier publishes reports without approval, and the third tier has employee-like access. SecureBio is a first-tier evaluator, currently reviewing a specific section of Anthropic’s risk report.
Anthropic is also exploring partnerships with other organizations, including Hugging Face, which was recently acquired by Nvidia for nearly $13 billion.

articles.title: Nvidia, AMD, Dell sink in global tech rout on AI funding worries
articles.preview: AI-related stocks experienced a significant downturn this week, with a combined loss of over $1 trillion. Concerns about financing for massive AI infrastructure projects are driving the sell-off across global tech companies.

summary.t: A wave of selling pressure impacted global tech stocks, particularly those involved in artificial intelligence and semiconductors. Twenty of the world’s most valuable AI and semiconductor stocks lost over $1 trillion this week. Nvidia, AMD, and Intel saw significant declines, with Nvidia dropping 1.84%, AMD falling 1.5%, and Intel losing approximately 2.8%.

The downturn extended beyond the United States, affecting markets across Asia and Europe. South Korean companies like SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics experienced sharp drops, with SK Hynix plunging more than 10% and Samsung Electronics decreasing by 8.73%. Japanese technology firms, including SoftBank Group and semiconductor equipment manufacturers, also saw substantial losses.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s statements eased some concerns within the AI trade.

articles.title: Bringing GPT-Rosalind to academic research labs
articles.preview: Rosalind, an AI coding assistant, is now available to academic research labs. This new plan provides sponsored access to GPT-Rosalind and related tools.

articles.title: Apple and Meta team up to make Muse AI model run on Mac computers
articles.preview: Apple and Meta are collaborating to allow developers to run Meta's Muse Spark Open AI model on Mac computers. This marks a surprising alliance between former rivals, driven by a shared interest in on-device AI capabilities.

summary.t: For years, Apple and Meta operated as competitors, marked by disagreements and a lack of public partnerships. Following John Ternus’s leadership at Apple, and after a period of animosity stemming from Apple’s privacy changes in 2021, the two companies are now collaborating. This collaboration represents a significant shift in the AI landscape, signaling a potential realignment of alliances within Silicon Valley.

summary.h: Muse Spark Open on Mac Studios
summary.t: Meta’s new open-weight AI model, Muse Spark Open, is designed to run on Apple’s high-end Mac Studio computers. The model, boasting 816 billion parameters and a mixture-of-experts architecture, can be downloaded and run locally, offering enhanced security and cost savings for users. The collaboration leverages Apple’s M5 Ultra chip and allows for pairing between two and four Mac Studio PCs to handle coding, video analysis, and agentic work.

Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang highlighted that many powerful open-weight models are too large for typical computers, but Mac Studios’ memory capacity makes Muse Spark Open practical. Developers can download the model from platforms like Hugging Face without complex configuration. Apple’s MLX AI framework is also being utilized to split the model across multiple machines. The company is offering benchmarks for its chips and technical documentation to support this effort.

Currently, a Mac Studio with the necessary M5 Ultra chip and 256GB of memory costs at least $10,799, with a more expensive version offering 512GB of RAM slated for release later this month. The collaboration aims to bring leading agent capabilities to desktop computers, and Meta’s developers have been purchasing hundreds of Mac computers for experimentation. This represents a significant investment for both companies.

articles.title: TSMC chip capacity is ‘fierce’ battleground for AI customers, amid record quarter
articles.preview: TSMC is facing intense competition for manufacturing capacity due to the booming artificial intelligence industry. The company’s record quarter highlights the unprecedented demand for its chips, creating a bottleneck in the industry’s growth.

summary.t: TSMC is experiencing a surge in demand driven by the artificial intelligence boom. The company’s record quarter demonstrates the scale of this need, with customers vying for limited manufacturing space. TSMC currently has the capacity to produce over 17 million 12-inch equivalent wafers annually, but this is insufficient to meet current requirements.

Several major tech firms, including Apple, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and OpenAI, rely on TSMC to produce custom AI accelerators. Competition for TSMC’s factory lines is described as ‘extremely fierce,’ with analysts reporting that TSMC receives at least 10 calls daily regarding wafer capacity. Nvidia, AMD, and Broadcom are also significant customers, often securing long-term contracts with TSMC.

TSMC is investing heavily in expanding its manufacturing capabilities, with plans for new fabs in Taiwan, Japan, and Arizona. This expansion totals $265 billion, and the company is considering a new facility in Texas. However, these projects will take years to complete, exacerbating current capacity constraints.
Analysts predict 102 new chip fabs will come online globally by 2029, with China expected to nearly triple its capacity by 2030.

articles.title: AWS, Anthropic race to deploy army of specialized engineers key to proving AI spending will pay off
articles.preview: Big Tech companies are investing heavily in specialized engineers to demonstrate the value of their artificial intelligence investments. Companies are deploying these engineers, called forward deployed engineers, to help businesses integrate AI technology and achieve measurable results.

summary.t: Several major tech firms are committing significant resources to building a workforce of specialized engineers – known as forward deployed engineers (FDEs). Amazon Web Services (AWS) has pledged $1 billion, OpenAI is investing over $4 billion, and Anthropic is dedicating $100 million. Accenture and Google Cloud are also building 1,000-person FDE teams, reflecting a widespread recognition of the need for hands-on AI deployment expertise.

The demand for FDEs is accelerating dramatically. U.S. job postings for this role surged from under 200 in 2023 to approximately 1,200 in 2025 and more than 7,300 in the first nine months of 2026. Median advertised salaries reached $195,456, representing a 40% increase from 2023 and a substantial premium compared to overall U.S. job postings.

Companies are taking different approaches to deploying FDEs. AWS is building its own organization, OpenAI is acquiring Tomoro, and Anthropic is training engineers within its customer base through a residency program. Accenture and Google Cloud are retraining experienced software engineers to focus on customer-facing AI deployment.

Experts emphasize that technical expertise alone is insufficient. FDEs must possess strong customer engagement skills, understand organizational dynamics, and navigate complex challenges. The residency program at Anthropic, modeled after medical education, highlights the need for practical experience and mentorship. While initial deployments show productivity gains, the ultimate test will be demonstrating tangible business returns, a goal that remains elusive based on current case studies.

articles.title: Teaching students to think and learn through questions
articles.preview: This article announces a new resource for teachers: ‘Celebrate Teachers’ Day with AI for Educators in Brazilian Portuguese.’ It highlights a ‘Study Mode’ feature designed to promote active learning.

articles.title: Deutlicher Gewinnsprung: Chip-Riese TSMC setzt Höhenflug fort
articles.preview: TSMC, der weltweit größte Auftragsfertiger für Halbleiter, hat einen enormen Gewinnanstieg verzeichnet. Dieser Erfolg ist vor allem auf den Boom der künstlichen Intelligenz zurückzuführen.

summary.t: TSMC hat im vergangenen Quartal einen Rekordgewinn von rund 21,02 Milliarden Euro erzielt, was einer Steigerung von 69 Prozent entspricht. Dies übertraf die Erwartungen der Analysten, die mit einem Ergebnis von rund 500 Millionen Euro gerechnet hatten.
Um dem steigenden Bedarf gerecht zu werden, plant TSMC Investitionen in Höhe von 52 bis 56 Milliarden Euro für den Ausbau seiner Produktionsanlagen.

articles.title: Anthropic's third-quarter revenue is said to hit $16.8 billion ahead of IPO
articles.preview: Anthropic announced record third-quarter revenue of $16.8 billion, fueling expectations for its upcoming IPO. The company is also reporting profitability and positive cash flow.

articles.title: An update on independent evaluators
articles.preview: Anthropic is taking steps to increase independent evaluation of its AI models and safety practices. The company has signed the White House Accord and is partnering with multiple third-party evaluators to assess potential risks.

summary.t: Anthropic has committed to stronger independent assessment of its models and safety practices. They’ve joined the White House Accord on Super Intelligence and are collaborating with multiple external auditors, including METR, SecureBio, and Accenture, to evaluate their systems.

Anthropic is working with METR, a nonprofit evaluator, granting them employee-like access to information. Six METR employees have been provided with company hardware and access. METR will publish the results of its risk assessments, aiming to close the gap in understanding between the company and external evaluators.

Anthropic is sharing sensitive information with evaluators to facilitate thorough risk assessments. However, certain categories of data, such as customer information or model architecture details, remain protected. Anthropic retains the right to redact information if necessary, but METR is free to publicly comment on these redactions.

Anthropic is developing a tiered system for evaluator access, starting with narrowly scoped investigations and progressing to full publication rights. This approach allows for controlled information sharing and ongoing refinement of the evaluation process. SecureBio is currently reviewing a specific section of the Risk Report, with plans for increased access as the review progresses.

articles.title: OpenAI sued by 8 states over ChatGPT safety concerns
articles.preview: Eight states have initiated legal action against OpenAI, citing safety concerns regarding its ChatGPT chatbot. The lawsuits allege the chatbot is harmful to children and misleading to parents.

summary.t: Iowa was the first state to file a lawsuit against OpenAI on Wednesday. Seven other states – Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho, and Montana – have followed suit, initiating separate legal proceedings in their respective state courts. Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird stated the lawsuit aims to protect Iowans from OpenAI’s alleged dangerous conduct.

The lawsuits accuse ChatGPT of providing dangerous medical advice, encouraging violence, and promoting suicide. Specifically, the states claim the chatbot is deceiving users, particularly children, and failing to adequately protect them from harm.

articles.title: Bank of America hired 1,000 contractors to patch software flaws exposed by Anthropic's Mythos
articles.preview: Bank of America has hired a large number of contractors to address vulnerabilities created by AI. The bank is investing heavily in software remediation efforts following the release of advanced AI models.

summary.t: Bank of America hired 1,000 contractors in the second quarter to address software flaws. This addition builds upon the existing 3,000 personnel already working in this area.

The bank spent a ‘couple hundred million plus’ on software remediation and related regulatory issues, particularly concerning anti-money laundering compliance. This expenditure occurred during the third quarter.

articles.title: Marktbericht: Europa wertvollster Konzern ASML macht KI-Boom möglich
articles.preview: ASML, Europas wertvollster Konzern, erlebt einen enormen Aufschwung aufgrund der Nachfrage nach KI-Infrastruktur. Dies führt zu einer Steigerung des Umsatzes und des Aktienwertes des Unternehmens.

summary.t: ASML verzeichnete im jüngsten Quartal einen Umsatz von knapp 11,7 Milliarden Euro, was eine deutliche Steigerung gegenüber den 9,3 Milliarden Euro des Vorquartals darstellt. Zudem verbesserte sich die Bruttomarge um 3,5 Prozentpunkte auf 57,5 Prozent und ASML verdiente knapp fünf Milliarden Euro. Diese Zahlen bestätigen den anhaltenden Erfolg des Unternehmens.

ASML stellt die einzigartigen Lithografiemaschinen her, die für die Produktion von KI-Halbleitern benötigt werden. Die Nachfrage nach diesen Maschinen treibt das Wachstum von ASML und ermöglicht den KI-Boom. Die Maschinen werden von großen Chipherstellern wie Apple, Nvidia und Samsung genutzt.
Investoren hinterfragen die Nachhaltigkeit des KI-Booms und die Rentabilität der bisherigen Investitionen. Volatilität und Abverkäufe bei Chip-Aktien zeigen die Unsicherheit auf dem Markt.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Tech-Werte mit Gegenbewegung nach Ausverkauf
Der Börsen-Tag: Abseits des Tech-Booms: Diese Aktien haben Potenzial
articles.preview: Die Technologieaktien, insbesondere im Bereich KI und Chips, erleben derzeit Turbulenzen. Dennoch gibt es auf der Börse weitere vielversprechende Aktien und Branchen, die von einer Fondsmanagerin vorgestellt werden.

articles.title: Ausverkauf wegen KI-Sorgen: Techwerte kommen von Tagestiefs zurück
articles.preview: Die Tech-Aktien haben aufgrund von Zinsängsten stark an Wert verloren, aber die Börsen kehren an den Abend wieder zu Ruhe zurück. Anleger konzentrierten sich auf defensivere Branchen während des Tages.

summary.t: Der Dow-Jones-Index schloss am Donnerstag mit einem Anstieg von 1,1 Prozent bei 52.177 Punkten. Der S&P 500 stieg um 0,3 Prozent auf 7744 Punkte. Der Nasdaq Index blieb kaum verändert, nachdem er im Handelstag zuvor 400 Punkte verloren hatte.

Unternehmen wie Eli Lilly, UnitedHealth und Walmart profitierten von Hochstufungen. Im Technologiebereich fielen Aktien von Broadcom und Nvidia, während Dell und Hewlett Packard Enterprise weiterhin an Wert verloren.

articles.title: Looking for non-AI stocks to own? Jim Cramer thinks these 2 names are worth buying
articles.preview: Jim Cramer is recommending investors consider apparel stocks VF Corp and Kontoor Brands despite concerns about rising interest rates. He believes these companies have significant upside potential due to shifting consumer trends.

summary.t: Jim Cramer is advising a purchase of VF Corp, citing a dramatic drop in its valuation. New research indicates a growing interest among teens in non-athletic footwear, particularly for Vans. Vans sales have declined nearly 50% since 2022, but the recent teen survey shows stabilization and a rise in popularity among male teens, particularly upper-income teens. The company's CEO, Bracken Darrell, is focused on improving Vans’ performance.

Jim Cramer also recommends Kontoor Brands, highlighting a potential resurgence in denim popularity. Jefferies has upgraded the stock to a buy rating with a price target of $89, anticipating Wrangler will benefit. Kontoor is also poised to gain from the planned sale of its Lee brand, valued up to $1 billion, and a $400 million share repurchase program.
Multiple analysts, including Truist and Piper Sandler, have raised their ratings on VF Corp, setting price targets of $20.

articles.title: CoreWeave credit default swaps hit distress levels as investors sour on AI debt
articles.preview: CoreWeave's debt obligations are facing increased investor concern, leading to a significant rise in credit default swap spreads. This distress is spreading across the AI-related investment landscape, impacting multiple companies.

summary.t: CoreWeave, having taken on over $51 billion in debt, is experiencing investor pushback due to worries about excessive AI spending. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 reached 15.78%, reflecting increased risk perceptions. Furthermore, the five-year credit default swap spread jumped 16% week-over-week, reaching nearly 1,038 basis points – a 164% increase year-over-year.

The distress at CoreWeave is impacting other ‘neocloud’ companies, with Nebius and Iren also experiencing stock declines. Alongside this, shares of Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices fell following broader sell-offs in South Korean chip stocks. Investors are now questioning the financial sustainability of companies heavily borrowing for AI infrastructure.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Techwerte-Ausverkauf juckt Dax nicht sonderlich
Viele Kurse fallen immer weiter: Ausverkauf von Tech-Aktien an US-Börsen vernichtet Billionenwerte
articles.preview: Die US-Börsen erleben einen massiven Ausverkauf von Technologieaktien. Die Stimmung ist durch Inflationssorgen und Zweifel an der KI-Finanzierung getrübt.

summary.t: Der Dow-Jones Index notierte am Morgen bei 51.755 Punkten, nachdem er zuvor 0,3 Prozent verloren hatte. Der S&P 500 verzeichnete einen Rückgang von 0,6 Prozent auf 7672 Zähler. Besonders deutlich fiel der Kursverfall der Technologiebörse Nasdaq aus, die um 1,4 Prozent auf 26.309 Punkte fiel.

Der Philadelphia Semiconductor Index verzeichnete Verluste von über zwei Billionen Dollar an Börsenwert nach sieben Verlusttagen in Folge. Die Anleger zeigen zunehmend Skepsis bezüglich der hohen Bewertungen von Technologieaktien.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Abseits des Tech-Booms: Diese Aktien haben Potenzial
articles.preview: Die Technologieaktien, insbesondere im Bereich KI und Chips, erleben derzeit Turbulenzen. Dennoch gibt es laut einer Fondsmanagerin interessante Anlagealternativen außerhalb des Tech-Booms.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Nasdaq mit knallrotem Start
Furcht vor einer Insolvenzwelle: Tech-Ausverkauf erfasst Europas Börsen
articles.preview: An der europäischen Börse herrscht ein dramatischer Ausverkauf im Technologiebereich. Die Anleger verlieren das Vertrauen in den KI-Boom und die steigenden Zinsen verschärfen die Situation.

summary.t: Vor allem Infineon, Aixtron und Suss Microtec erleiden erhebliche Kursverluste. Der DAX fiel um rund ein halbes Prozent, der EuroStoxx50 um rund ein Prozent. Die Aktien der genannten Unternehmen sanken um acht bis neun Prozent. Die Nervosität der Anleger wurde durch die überraschend hohen US-Verbraucherpreise verstärkt.

Auch in Asien und den USA gab es massive Verluste im Technologiesektor. Der japanische und südkoreanische Nikkei 225 Index fielen um rund 5 und 7,5 Prozent. Der Nasdaq in den USA verzeichnete einen Rückgang von knapp zwei Prozent.

articles.title: Marktbericht: TSMC gibt sich keine Blöße
articles.preview: TSMC hat einen neuen Rekordgewinn erzielt. Die Nachfrage nach Chips, insbesondere im Zusammenhang mit dem KI-Boom, ist weiterhin extrem hoch.

summary.t: Der taiwanische Chip-Auftragsfertiger TSMC hat einen Umsatz von 41,66 Milliarden Euro erzielt, was einen Anstieg von 50 Prozent gegenüber dem Vorjahr darstellt. Das Unternehmen prognostiziert ein Wachstum von 55 bis 61 Prozent für das laufende Quartal und einen Gesamtjahresumsatzanstieg von 44 Prozent.

Die hohe Nachfrage nach Chips wird maßgeblich durch den KI-Boom getrieben. Unternehmen wie Nvidia, Samsung und ASML generieren Rekordergebnisse, was die Kapazitäten von TSMC überlastet. Das Unternehmen plant, seine Produktionskapazitäten massiv auszubauen.

TSMC bestätigte seine Investitionsziele von 64 Milliarden Dollar für 2026. Analysten äußern jedoch Bedenken hinsichtlich der hohen Zinsen, die mit der Finanzierung von Rechenzentren verbunden sind. Die Angst vor einer Überbewertung der KI-Aktien ist groß.

articles.title: Memory stocks are getting hammered. China and a 2029 oversupply are the big worries
articles.preview: Memory chip stocks are experiencing a significant downturn. Concerns about Chinese competition and potential oversupply are driving the market’s decline.

summary.t: Several memory chip stocks, including SK Hynix (-26%), Samsung (-22%), and Micron (-11%), have dropped sharply. This decline is fueled by worries about Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT’s new server memory product with higher storage density, potentially leading to market share shifts.

Analysts question CXMT’s ability to scale production due to potential low yields. Ben Barringer highlighted the issue of chip yield, stating that a 50% yield would result in significant chip waste. Kevin Cassidy confirmed that CXMT’s developments wouldn’t significantly impact supply.

A Maeil Business Newspaper opinion column predicted a memory market oversupply in 2029, citing Professor Hwang and Ahn Ki-hyun. The article warned of a ‘flood of new supply’ potentially turning the market into a ‘red ocean’ by 2030, leading to an industry downturn.

summary.h: Musk’s Prediction and Long Lead Times
summary.t: Elon Musk responded to the article on X, predicting a large increase in RAM production by China in 2028.

articles.title: TSMC posts record profit for a sixth straight quarter, beating estimates on AI boom
articles.preview: TSMC achieved record profits for the sixth consecutive quarter, driven by strong demand for AI chips. The company’s performance significantly exceeded analyst expectations, signaling continued growth in the semiconductor industry.

summary.t: TSMC announced a record net profit for the third quarter, representing a 68.7% increase compared to the same period last year. This marks the sixth consecutive quarter of record profitability for the world’s largest contract chipmaker.

The company’s operating margin reached 58.7%, surpassing its own guidance. TSMC projects fourth-quarter revenue between $52.3 billion and $54.3 billion, a 14% sequential increase and a 58% jump from the previous year. Significant capital expenditure is planned through 2028 to meet growing demand.

Advanced technologies, particularly those at 7 nanometers and beyond, accounted for 79% of TSMC’s total wafer revenue. 3-nanometer chips dominated revenue in the third quarter, followed by 5- and 7-nanometer chips. High-performance computing and smartphones were the largest revenue contributors by platform.

articles.title: Sorge wegen hoher Inflation: Tech-Werte rutschen an der Wall Street ab
articles.preview: Die Technologiebranche an der Wall Street hat stark an Wert verloren. Hohe Inflationszahlen haben die Befürchtungen vor einer Zinserhöhung der US-Notenbank Fed verstärkt.

summary.t: Die US-Verbraucherpreise sind im September stärker gestiegen als erwartet. Der Anstieg wurde hauptsächlich durch teures Benzin und einen allgemeinen Preisdruck verursacht. Die Jahresinflationsrate liegt aktuell bei 3,7 Prozent, was höher ist als ursprünglich prognostiziert.
Die überraschend hohen Inflationsdaten haben die Wahrscheinlichkeit einer weiteren Zinserhöhung durch die US-Notenbank Fed auf 37 Prozent erhöht.

articles.title: Traders pile into 'bubble puts' on CoreWeave as neocloud stocks plunge
articles.preview: Traders are heavily investing in ‘bubble puts’ on CoreWeave, a key AI infrastructure provider, amid a downturn in neocloud stocks. This surge in put options suggests expectations of a significant decline in CoreWeave’s value.

summary.t: Shares of CoreWeave, a company providing GPU access for AI, experienced a dramatic drop of 15% on Wednesday. This decline followed rising debt yields for Nvidia-backed CoreWeave, fueled by reports of the company seeking further debt financing.

Trading volume in options related to CoreWeave, Nebius Group, and Iren surged dramatically. CoreWeave saw over seven times its 30-day average volume, Nebius almost four times, and Iren twice the normal volume.

articles.title: CoreWeave shares tumble as bond yields near 15% on concern about AI borrowing binge
articles.preview: CoreWeave's stock and bonds experienced a significant drop as investors worried about technology companies' heavy borrowing for artificial intelligence projects. Bond yields for CoreWeave have risen sharply, reflecting increased investor concern.

summary.t: CoreWeave's debt yields have surged dramatically. The 9.625% bond due in 2032 now carries a yield of 14.8%, while the 9.75% bond due in 2031 is at 14.9%. Investor demand for risk compensation has increased, driven by concerns about the scale of AI-related borrowing.

Analysts point to CoreWeave's balance sheet as a contributing factor. Paul Meeks of Freedom Capital Markets noted that CoreWeave has taken on more debt and is building more data centers than its peers. The company’s credit rating is currently a B+ at S&P Credit Ratings, considered junk bond territory. “The yields have blown out because there’s just more and more concern — that I don’t share — about the wherewithal of these guys [being] able to over time pay back their interest expense.”
The concerns surrounding AI borrowing have impacted the broader tech sector. Shares of Oracle fell nearly 9%, and Nebius dropped 10%.

articles.title: Dell stock plunges 11%, leading data center sell-off as fears mount about 'enterprise AI timing'
articles.preview: Dell stock experienced a significant drop, and several other data center companies saw declines. Concerns are growing about the timing of enterprise investment in artificial intelligence.

summary.t: Dell shares fell by 11% on Wednesday, triggering a broader downturn in the data center equipment sector. This decline followed a Barclays downgrade of Dell, HPE, and NetApp, citing concerns about enterprise AI spending.
Hewlett-Packard Enterprise, Oracle, and Super Micro also experienced significant drops. Neocloud CoreWeave fell 15%, erasing its gains for the year.

articles.title: Inflation data, Bank of America's penalty, Apple's new home hub and more in Morning Squawk
articles.preview: Inflation data is set to be released this morning, with economists anticipating a resurgence in price growth. Simultaneously, Bank of America faces a significant penalty from the U.S.

summary.t: Bank of America's stock price fell over 4% in premarket trading following a $1.2 billion penalty from the U.S. Treasury Department. The penalty stemmed from alleged violations of anti-money laundering and sanctions laws. This resulted in a 17-cent per share reduction in income. CEO Brian Moynihan is facing scrutiny regarding the bank's oversight.

Morgan Stanley reported equities trading revenue numbers exceeding analyst expectations by more than $900 million. This positive performance contrasts with Bank of America's disappointing results. Brian Moynihan and Ted Pick will discuss these developments on CNBC’s ‘Squawk on the Street’ today.
